title: 13A Dredge Material Containment Area (DMCA) Dike Raising and Weir Improvements
description: This is a Sources Sought/Request for Information Only. This is not a Solicitation Annoucement, nor is it a Request for Proposal.. This does not obligate the Government in any contract award. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District is issuing the sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirements as stated in the scope of work. The results of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 237990 - Dredging and Surface Clean Up Activities) with a size standard of $37,000,000.00. The Product Service Code is Z1KF - Maintenance of Dredging Facilities. Savannah Harbor is located at Savannah on the northern coast of Georgia / southern coast of South Carolina in Chatham and Jasper Counties, respectively. The Savannah River is the line of demarcation separating Georgia from South Carolina. Savannah Harbor Dredge Material Containment Area (DMCA) 13A, located along and to the north of the Savannah River North Channel across from Elba Island, lies in Jasper County, South Carolina. The area is one of nine confined dredge material containment areas used for dredging the Savannah River channel. The containment area is roughly 1,380 acres in size and parallels the Savannah River beginning at approximate channel station 48+000 and extending south-west to channel station 58+000 and then along the Back River Channel from station 0+000 to about station 6+500.DMCA 13A is located between DMCA 12A and DMCA 13B. Dikes have been constructed around the entire perimeter of this area for confined storage of dredging materials. Although the area has not always had dikes, it has received dredged materials from the Savannah River throughout the 1900�s. The disposal area is drained using a series of water control structures (weirs). The six weirs are located along the backside of DMCA 13A and empty into the marsh. Two of the six weirs are blanked off. The dikes are periodically raised as needed to increase capacity for dredge spoils. Savannah Harbor DMCA 13A will be used primarily for disposal of the O&M maintenance dredging materials that will be excavated during dredging of the Savannah River. In order to safely contain these materials, the capacity of DMCA 13A needs to be increased and improvements to the water control outlets need to be made. The Scope of Work for this project consists of raising the DMCA 13A perimeter back dike, repairs and modifications to four of the six existing weir/water control structures across the back (marsh-side) dike, and the expansion of the bird island. The existing back dike currently spans a length of approximately 10,600 feet and has a crest elevation of approximately 46 feet MLLW. After extending the interior counterweight, the back dike will be raised to a uniform crest elevation of 52 feet MLLW to gain additional capacity for containment of Savannah Harbor dredged material. The existing 13A/13B cross dike currently spans a length of approximately 2,500 feet and has a crest elevation ranging from about 46 to 51 feet MLLW. After extending the interior counterweight for the span, the cross dike will be raised to a crest elevation that varies from 52 feet MLLW in the back to an elevation of 57 feet MLLW at the front. The existing 13A/12A cross dike currently spans a length of approximately 4,800 feet and has a crest elevation ranging from about 52 to 55 feet MLLW. The cross dike will be raised to a crest elevation that varies from 52 feet MLLW in the back to an elevation of 57 feet MLLW at the front. The existing front dike currently spans a length of approximately 16,200 feet and has a crest elevation ranging from about 51 to 52 feet MLLW. The front dike will be raised to a uniform crest elevation of 57 feet MLLW. The fill material for raising the dikes will be obtained from the interior of DMCA 13A. Repairs and modifications to the existing weirs will involve temporary removal, replacement of corroded steel, reinforcement of the outfall stub, the addition of a new bonneted knife gate valves, a new larger weir platform, a catwalk extension, and re-installation on a new slab foundation. The Period of Performance is 540 days from Notice to Proceed. If you are interested in this project and/or your organization has the potential capacity to perform these services, please submit the following to the Point of Contact listed below: 1. Name and Address of Your Firm 2. Point of Contact (Name/Phone/Email) 3. Company Website 4. Unique Entity ID 5. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE code (https://cage.dla.mil) 6. Business Size, to include designation as HUBZone, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business (SOB), Woman-Owned Business, and Large Business. The Government must be able to verify SBA certification of HUBZone, 8(a), and SOB via the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov/) and the Small Business Dynamic Search (https://dsbs.sba .gov /sea rch/dsp _dsbs.cfm) \ 7. title: Solid-State Energy Conversion from Heat to Electricity Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Defense Sciences Office (DSO) is requesting information on the current state of the art and technological limitations of solid-state direct thermal-to-electric energy conversion technologies. We define solid state energy conversion as systems that convert a temperature differential directly into electrical energy without utilizing mechanical moving parts (e.g., pistons, turbines, or rotary alternators). This RFI seeks to identify the best possible solid state heat engine performance across a wide operating temperature range, factors that limit performance, and the most attractive use cases if these highly efficient solid state heat engines could be made today. This survey of limits, challenges and use cases will identify opportunities for research and development to inform potential program(s) in this area.

description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE AEC11 Source control (design bid build) 19 wing, CFB Comox, Lazo, BC (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at 19 Wing, CFB Comox, Lazo, BC. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN or Contract Number: 87758 Approximate Estimate: $9,300,000 Anticipated Posting: January 2027 Description: Remediation of PFAS-impacted soils at CFB Comox through in-situ soil mixing (chemical) and stabilization, selective excavation, off-site disposal, drainage improvements, and site restoration. The work is located within a former detonation and training area and is subject to UXO risk, environmental protection requirements, and tight seasonal construction windows. Construction will be completed in two distinct phases due to schedule constraints, UXO sequencing, and constructability considerations. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. title: Ireland – Real estate agency services on a fee or contract basis – Real Estate Consultancy Services Frameworks for Public Transport, Roads, Greenways and Active Travel Projects
description: Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) intends to establish four-year multi-supplier Real Estate Consultancy Services Frameworks (Lot 1 and 2) to provide a broad range of property, valuation, land acquisition, compensation, estate management, development, regeneration, and related advisory services in support of its infrastructure programmes and corporate property requirements. This competition will comprise of two lots: Lot 1 – Public Transport and Corporate Services This Lot will provide multi-disciplinary real estate consultancy services to support TII's public transport programmes and corporate property portfolio. Public transport projects include light rail, metro and other transport infrastructure projects delivered by TII under its remit from the National Transport Authority. The Framework will be available to TII and any statutory delivery body established for the delivery of MetroLink. Key services include: Property acquisition, disposal and leasing Valuation and compensation advice CPO support services Property negotiations and stakeholder engagement Estate and asset management Development and regeneration advice Rating and taxation services Facilities management Expert witness and dispute resolution services Planning, environmental and specialist property advisory services Estimated value: €12.5 million to €15.75 million. Lot 2 – Major and Minor Roads, Greenways and Active Travel This lot will support the planning and delivery of roads, greenway and active travel projects nationwide and will be available to both TII and Local Authorities. Key services include: Land and property valuation Land acquisition and compensation Agricultural and agronomy advice Accommodation works assessments Wayleave and rights-of-way acquisition Stakeholder and landowner negotiations Land cost estimation and risk assessment CPO support and compensation claim management Arbitration and expert witness services Mapping, land transfer and close-out reporting Estimated value: €9.1 million to €12 million.

title: Balfour Beatty - Roads North of the Thames-LTC - Technology Disconnections and Street Lighting Diversions
description: We are inviting expressions of interest from experienced suppliers for Technology Disconnections and Street Lighting Diversions on the Lower Thames Crossing Roads North programme. The works support the Roads North Temporary Diversions (RNoT), including the A13 and M25 temporary diversion routes. Package Scope The package includes, but is not limited to: Technology disconnections, diversions and alteration works on the M25. Street lighting diversions and alterations on the M25, A13, A1089 and associated side roads. Disconnection, relocation, modification and reconnection of street lighting and technology assets. Alterations to lighting feeder pillars, electrical supplies, cabling and associated infrastructure. Alterations and diversions to technology electrical infrastructure (EI). Installation, relocation or replacement of lighting columns, luminaires, cabling and equipment. Testing, inspection, commissioning and certification of completed works. Managing temporary and permanent arrangements to maintain safe operation of affected systems. Producing test certification, commissioning records and as-built information. Coordinating with the Contractor, Design Team and stakeholders to meet programme and design requirements. Suppliers should be able to: Deliver highway technology disconnections, diversions and street lighting works on operational road networks. Undertake electrical isolation, installation, testing and commissioning. Demonstrate experience working safely on live highways, including strategic roads and motorways. Manage interfaces with existing highway technology and lighting infrastructure. Provide robust quality assurance and testing processes. Deliver within challenging programme and traffic management constraints. Work collaboratively with Tier 1 contractors, designers and stakeholders. Experience & Standards We are looking for companies with: Proven experience delivering street lighting diversions and highway technology works on major infrastructure projects. Experience in feeder pillar alterations, circuit modifications, electrical disconnections/reconnections and lighting works. Appropriately qualified personnel for electrical installation, isolation, inspection, testing and commissioning. Strong health, safety, environmental and quality management systems. Experience working within National Highways and/or local authority environments. Ability to meet Lower Thames Crossing requirements relating to sustainability, carbon reduction and social value. We actively welcome expressions of interest from SMEs with the relevant experience and capability. Next Steps If you are interested and would like further information, including pre-qualification requirements and tender timelines, please respond by 23.11.26. Additional information: The Lower Thames Crossing (LTC) is a new road to better connect Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive a change in how we deliver - connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, leaving a skills legacy for the local community and construction industry, all whilst restoring nature and drawing a new blueprint for low-carbon construction. Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road, and to do the right thing for local communities and the environment. We can only achieve this with the support of our supply chain, and it is therefore critical that for any supplier to be successful in winning work on LTC, they must demonstrate commitments to supporting delivery of our ambitions: • Delivering the works through a 'zero emissions' solution, and not using diesel on site in any plant or machinery. • Supporting us to leave a skills legacy for the local community, by not only recruiting locally, but upskilling your workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher paid higher skilled work. • Helping to facilitate successful opportunities by providing early careers roles, as well as inspiring young people into construction through delivery of STEM engagement.

title: Service Order Desk
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT FOR SOLUTION BASED CAPABILITY STATEMENTS ONLY. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) - Fort Carson, CO, in coordination with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), is seeking Solution based capability statement for an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Market Research purposes. The requirement is to design, integrate, test, deploy, and support a modernized, commercial Service Order Desk Platform. The core objective is to decouple the Service Order Desk from the legacy Base Operations contract, transitioning it into an independent, highly automated, data-transparent, and user-centric platform. Successful solutions must deliver 100% auditable real-time tracking of funds by facility type, establish direct digital pathways with the Army Maintenance Application (ArMA) without manual data re-entry, and prevent premature ticket closures via multi-state tracking and parallel POC notifications.. Security compliance requires deployment in a secure Department of War (DOW) Impact Level 5 (IL5) cloud environment featuring Role-Based Access Control and CAC/SSO integration . Submissions must be Solution Based Capability Statement not exceeding 10 pages and must be submitted by Monday, November 23, 2026, at 10:00 AM MT to Jessica Smith (Jessica.l.smith499.civ@army.mil), Frank Camacho (frank.m.camacho.civ@army.mil), and MAJ Ryan Lee (jong.d.lee2.mil@army.mil) ====A0001==== This amendment formally establishes the deadline for receipt of industry questions. All questions must be submitted no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 1000 Hours MT. Questions with answers will be posted Tuesday, November 10, 2026 by 1000 Hours MT. ====A0001====

title: Optos California Service Agreement
description: SAM.gov SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Solicitation Number: 75N98027Q00082 Title: Optos California Service Agreement Classification Code: J066 NAICS Code: 811210 - Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance Description: Maintenance and repair service for imaging devices. This is a Small Business Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should not submit a response to this notice. This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified companies technically capable of meeting the Government requirement and to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Background: The Imaging Services Section of the National Eye Institute (NEI) produces digital clinical images in support of the Intramural Research Program (IRP). Three types of Optos California instruments are employed by NEI for these services including ultra-wide-field (UWF) color fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence, and angiography. NEI utilizes four (4) devices in total: California ICG (1) Monaco (1) California FA (2) Purpose and Objectives: The NIH, Office of Logistics and Acquisitions Operations (OLAO), intends to award a comprehensive service contract to ensure the continued operational readiness and reliability of four (4) Optos ultrawide-widefield (U-WF) imaging devices. Project requirements: Independently, and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall perform the following: Service Visits Provide on-site Emergency and Planned Maintenance support during the term of the agreement. At each planned maintenance visit, perform all planned maintenance per Optos System Service Manual. At each Emergency Service event, repair the system, including parts as required, to a fully functioning state. Relocate systems if necessary. Service Hours Provide service visits between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday (excludes Holidays), at no charge. Provide an on-site technician within 48 hours of receiving a request from NEI. Off-Hours Emergency Support Anticipated period of performance: January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2027 Requested Response: The intent of this sources sought notice is to help define the procurement strategy (e.g., set-aside, sole source, unrestricted) for a solicitation intended to be posted at a later date. Interested contractors are requested to respond by (1) describing their relevant experience and capability to perform surveillance/quality assurance services of the kind described above, including not less than five years of experience in Quality Assurance Inspections/Surveillance related to the security field and performance-based contracts; and (2) providing a capability statement demonstrating their bona fide ability to perform this requirement within the time frame described above. In addition, please state your business size status and whether you maintain, or would be able to establish, an administrative office within 100 miles of the NIH campus. Please note that NIH is particularly interested in small business sources. If you are a small business, please state the type of small business (small business; HUBZone; service-disabled, veteran-owned; 8(a); veteran-owned; woman-owned; or small disadvantaged businesses) and your size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The respondent must also provide their Unique Entity ID (UEI), organization name, address, point of contact, and size and type of business (e.g., 8(a), HubZone, etc.), pursuant to the applicable NAICS code and any other information that may be helpful in developing or finalizing the acquisition requirements. The information submitted must be must be in an outline format that addresses each of the elements of the project requirements and in the capability statement /information sought paragraphs stated herein. A cover page and an executive summary may be included but is not required. The response must include the respondents� technical and administrative points of contact, including names, titles, addresses, telephone and fax numbers, and e-mail addresses. All responses to this notice must be submitted electronically. Facsimile responses are NOT accepted. Responses must be submitted to: Gannon White, Contracting Officer - gannon.white@nih.gov Responses must be received on or before: Monday, November 23, 2026, 12:00pm (Eastern) Disclaimer and Important Notes: This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization�s qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. title: Canonsburg-Houston, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District, has a project as the Canonsburg-Houston Local Protection Project (LPP) is an authorized federal flood damage reduction project spanning over 20,500 linear feet of channel improvements along Chartiers Creek. Originally constructed by USACE in two phases (Houston unit completed in 1970; Canonsburg unit completed in 1976), operation and maintenance responsibilities were subsequently transferred to Washington County. Severe storm events resulted in substantial damage to the channel embankment along the right bank of Chartiers Creek, including displacement of stone protection and loss of subgrade stabilization. This rehabilitation contract encompasses repair and re-armoring of the degraded channel reach to restore federal project integrity and design conveyance capacity. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $150,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 11 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/ then scrolling down on right hand side of page by clicking on View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

title: AFP for Lease of Discovery Park at Michoud Assembly Facility
description: This Announcement for Proposals (AFP) solicits proposals for lease of Discovery Park which represents a selection of available real property assets at MAF. The real property assets (The Property) known as Discovery Park, and shown in Exhibit A, are as follows: 1. Approximately 45 Acres of Greenspace: This tract of land lies on the northern extent of the facility and is bounded by Old Gentilly Road (publicly accessible roadway) as well as Mercury, Uranus and Venus Drives, which are interior to the security fencing. The acreage is currently classified as underutilized greenspace. The tract�s frontage to Old Gentilly Road has availability to direct connection with municipal power, potable water and sewer services. These utilities may be established with each respective service carrier. Please see Exhibit B for a listing of municipal resources which may assist in performing diligence for these service agreements. The acreage includes what were previously large sections of parking areas that supported a previously demolished building. These areas are past their useful service life and thus have been considered greenspace for appraisal purposes. 2. Building 351: Building 351 is an approximately 32,000 sf mixed used facility. The building is subdivided into two main areas: formal event space and cafeteria. The building currently is connected to the MAF utility grids. As a result, some determination will need to be made with respect to severing the building from those utilities and re-establishing utility services from the previously mentioned municipal service providers based upon the proposer�s concept of use. This reconfiguration would be made subject to NASA�s approval and terms of use. The Proposer may choose to propose on either asset separately or a combination of the two. NASA shall have the authority to execute either one or multiple leases in the event The Proposer chooses to include a combination of both assets in their submission. NASA intends to utilize Enhanced Use Lease authority as set forth in 51 U.S.C. 20145 as the sole means to enter into a lease(s) for The Property. The Proposer will assume any and all financial responsibilities for operations and maintenance of The Property under such a lease. The terms and conditions in the attached Model Enhanced Use Lease (EUL) generally demonstrate all the Proposer responsibilities including those maintenance and operational parameters. While The Property has existing utilities which serve other portions of the facility, the Proposer should not assume that any existing utilities will be available for use and that any utilities required for development will be at the sole cost of the Proposer. The Property will be available at award in �as is� condition for no less than one ten (10) year base term. title: Dry Dock Inspection, Repair, Hull Cleaning and Repainting of up to Six Vessels
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - St. Paul District is seeking contractors to transport, dry dock, water blast/clean, inspect, repair and repaint six (6) vessels - four (4) unpowered barges and two (2) 43 ft push boat/dredge tender motor vessels. The vessels will be picked up at Lock and Dam 7 - La Crescent, MN (UMRM 702.5), moved to the shipyard, and returned to the same location. One of the barges requires deck replacement and significant structural repairs. Both motor vessels (M/V Hooper and M/V Lyon) require non-destructive testing (NDT - i.e. ultrasonic thickness [UT]) of hulls and complete mechanical and running gear inspection and servicing. Contractor will prepare condition reports and itemized cost estimates for all repairs not explicitly stated in SOW. The Government will issue contract modifications to authorize the additional repairs when the requirements and pricing are known. Contractor is not permitted to operate vessels under their own power. This solicitation may result in multiple firm-fixed price contract awards. Offers will be evaluated based on the price per vessel, shipyard capacity, and past performance, with price being the most important consideration. This solicitation is 100% set-aside for small businesses under NAICS 336611, with an SBA size standard of 1,300 employees. This solicitation may result in multiple contract awards, based on the following factors (in order of importance): Price for each vessel, shipyard capacity, past performance. Interested parties are requested to submit any questions through the PIEE module Q and A section. Offerors are requested to submit their quotes through the PIEE module. Links to the PIEE module and for PIEE Registration are in the Attachments/Links section.

title: REMEDIATION AND RESTORATION ACTIVITIES
description: Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Department of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Facilities Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program. As part of this effort, a Remedial Action (RA) will be conducted at one facility in the FAA Eastern Service Area (ESA) to remove identified soil contamination. The site requiring remediation for lead- and polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-contaminated soils is QPI RCAG � Matawan, NJ (40.370895�,-74.220954�). The FAA�s ECU Program has identified the potential for environmental and human health risks and/or liability associated with the facility above based on prior research, known historic operations and practices, and required cleanup actions. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State, and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. The Contractor shall submit a draft Remediation and Restoration work plan (Work Plan) (where applicable) within ten (10) business days of the project kick-off meeting that addresses the project requirements below. This task involves the preparation and submission of a draft and final Work Plan. The Work Plan shall detail the technical approach and schedule for conducting all contaminated soil remediation, disposal, and site restoration activities described below. To assist with preparation of the Work Plan, the contractor shall thoroughly review the Government-furnished information (GFI) for pertinent information. The removal quantities and depths in the Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation and Remedial Investigation reports (if provided) are to be used as a guide along with the estimated total quantities listed in this SOW Section 2.2.2. The Work Plan shall describe methods and procedures for performing soil remediation, disposal, and restoration. Disposal methods must be detailed by the contractor for the site. FAA has consulted a Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP), and the LSRP will select and approve all disposal facilities where waste and debris is to be shipped. Disposal sampling and paperwork is the responsibility of the contractor. Confirmatory sampling has already been conducted at the site. Additionally, the work plan shall also identify any required permits needed to perform the work. Futhermore, components required with the Work Plan are the Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP), which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed. The work plan shall also include a brief Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards on each site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. An outline summarizing the required content of the work plan is Technical Approach (Method and procedures for soil remediation, removal, disposal a. Identification of required work permits and b. Site Safety Health Plan (SSHP). Risk Management Plan a. Identification of major risks and b.Risk mitigation plan. The contractor should expect a 5-business day Volpe Center review period between submission of the Draft Work Plan and receipt of Volpe Center comments. The Volpe Center and the Contractor shall meet to discuss any comments and changes, if necessary. The contractor shall make the changes and submit a Final Work Plan within 5 business days of the receipt of comments. Contaminated Soil Remediation: Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation (PA/SI) and Remedial Investigation (RI) activities completed between 2020 and 2025 found soils at the below site containing contamination above FAA�s action levels, which are based on U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and/or New Jersey Residential Soil Remediation Standards. Examples include lead-in-soil concentrations above 200 mg/kg (ppm) or PCB-in-soil concentrations above 0.25 mg/kg. See SOW for greater details.

title: Sources Sought: IEE/ISBEE Capability Inquiry � CRNA Services � Turtle Mountain Service Unit, Quentin N. Burdick Memorial Healthcare Facility, Belcourt, ND.
description: Sources Sought: IHS1532109 � CRNA Services � Turtle Mountain Service Unit, Quentin N. Burdick Memorial Healthcare Facility, Belcourt, ND The Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks capability information from Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs), small businesses, and other responsible sources for up to two qualified Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs) at Quentin N. Burdick Memorial Healthcare Facility, Belcourt, North Dakota 58316. Services include inpatient, outpatient, and emergency anesthesia care for patients of all ages within approved scope and facility-granted privileges. Anticipated assignments are fourteen-day blocks, staffed by one CRNA for fourteen days or two CRNAs for seven days each, with usual weekday clinical hours of 7:00 a.m.�3:30 p.m. and scheduled night, weekend, and Federal holiday on-call and call-back coverage. Assignment frequency and coverage between blocks remain under development. Respondents should recommend feasible schedules and identify whether their approach covers assigned blocks only or continuous coverage. IHS anticipates a firm-fixed-price contract for commercial, non-personal healthcare services, priced by Month (MO), including defined clinical and call coverage and associated contractor costs. The tentative start date is February 1, 2027, with a six-month base period and four six-month option periods. Dates and final requirements are subject to change. Services may begin only after award and required onboarding, credentialing, and privileging. The anticipated NAICS code is 621399 � Offices of All Other Miscellaneous Health Practitioners, with a small business size standard of $10 million in average annual receipts, subject to Contracting Officer confirmation. Respondents may recommend alternatives with supporting rationale. Responses will inform acquisition planning, including consideration of a Buy Indian Act set-aside under 25 U.S.C. 47 and applicable HHSAR requirements. No set-aside determination is announced. Review the full Sources Sought Notice, draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) in this SAM.gov notice�s attachments/links. Capability statements should address: Business name, address, UEI, CAGE code if available, SAM.gov registration status, business size under the anticipated NAICS code, socioeconomic status, and contact information. IEE/ISBEE status, if claimed, including the current IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form and identified Tribe(s). Comparable anesthesia staffing experience, including rural or remote coverage. Staffing capacity, provider availability, mobilization lead time, credentialing support, replacement coverage, safe scheduling, and ability to meet the draft PWS and QASP. Applicable contract vehicles and recommended requirement changes. Optional nonbinding, all-inclusive monthly budget estimates identifying coverage days, rotations, coverage between blocks, clinical and call obligations, and base/option price differences. Price alternative approaches separately. Hourly quotations and formal proposals are not requested. Submit responses by November 23, 2026, at noon Central Time to David.Jones@ihs.gov using the subject line: Sources Sought Notice: IHS1532109 � CRNA Services � Belcourt ND Limit responses to ten single-sided pages, including attachments, in Word or PDF, with at least 12-point font, letter-size pages, and one-inch margins. Mark proprietary information. Do not submit patient information, Social Security numbers, banking information, or individual provider health records. This notice is for market research only. It is not a solicitation or Government commitment. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted for award. Response costs will not be reimbursed, and submission does not guarantee a solicitation or award. Contact: David Jones, Contract Specialist, IHS Great Plains Area, Division of Acquisition Management; David.Jones@ihs.gov.

title: Float Well Pipe Repairs, Surry Mountain Dam, Surry, NH
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the for the repairing of the inlet pipe to the float well and replace weathered/damaged staff gauges at the Surry Moutain Lake Dam in Surry NH. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990 with a size standard of $45M. The project is planned to be solicited in the Winter of 2026 with construction to begin place in the Summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $350,000 - $500,000. The project site is the inlet culvert on the lake side of the Surry Mountain Dam in Surry, NH. Work for this project will likely include, but not be limited to, the following: Coffer dam at inlet pipe location. Float well pipe (3-inch cast iron) cleaning. Installation of internal liner for float well pipe. Pre and Post liner installation CCTV inspections. Repairs to the slash-zone pipe segment Protection and concrete encasement of the external float well pipe Staff Gauges: Pressure treated posts with attached enamel coated metal measuring strip. Scheduled work will be affected by depth of pool. Assumed low pool depths are July and August (when work can be conducted safely), but adverse weather conditions (rain events) could delay or postpone work schedules. Surry Mountain staff will keep COR informed of pool levels to anticipate when work can commence if outside assumed low pool depths. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. Please include at least two specific examples of the firm�s experience performing the work requirements stated above. The projects must have been performed within the last seven years. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications, which will be used to support the offeror�s effort, and their experience must also have been performed within the last seven years. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by 21 September 2026. Responses should be emailed to: Kyle Hall � kyle.k.hall@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8479 Interested firms shall provide the above documentation in one original form and one copy. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. title: INL Serbia Shooting Range Simulator System
description: The International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Section of the Embassy of the United States of America in Serbia supports procurement of a scenario-based laser shooting range system and complementary tactical preparedness and response police training kits to complete new training facilities at University or Criminal Investigation and Police Studies in Belgrade, Serbia. This training solution will provide controlled, analytical training environment needed to assess, document, and translate scenario-based tactical instruction into measurable performance improvements, institutional accountability and long-term learning. SUBSTANTIVE REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall fulfill the following substantive requirements (See Attachment A RFQ/SOW for a complete listing of requirements/quantities): I LASER TRAINING SIMULATOR SYSTEM II SIMULATION TRAINING CENTRE - TRAINING KITS III INSTALLATION/TRAINING � ONSITE INTERNATIONAL Delivery The vendor is responsible for the delivery of all items. The vendor shall consolidate the entire shipment to prevent loss and misdirection. Entire shipment must be consolidated at the origin and shipped consolidated, partial shipments are not accepted by post due to the Serbian customs donation regulations. Entire shipment must be consolidated under one AWB or CMR. Any lost or damaged items during shipment shall be replaced by the contractor upon notification. Packaging and preservation shall be IAW best commercial practices to enable shipment to final destination in Serbia to the address specified (see Attachment A RFQ/SOW), without repacking or incurring damage during shipment and handling. Delivery shall be made FOB Destination as soon as possible but not later than 90 days from the date of contract award. Submission Requirements (please see details in the Attachment A � RFQ/SOW) Evaluation Criteria (please see details in the Attachment A � RFQ/SOW) After initial evaluation of quotes, the Contracting Officer may negotiate final terms with one or more contractors of the Government�s choice before issuing a purchase order. The Contracting Officer will not negotiate with any contractors other than those of the Government�s choice and will not use the formal source selection procedures described in FAR Part 15. The Government may perform a comparative evaluation to select the contractor that provides the best value, considering the evaluation factors below. The Contracting Officer may issue a purchase order to other than the contractor with the lowest proposed price. The Government will consider the following factors when selecting contractors for award. The following factors shall be used to evaluate quotes: 1) Technical Specifications: Quote must meet or exceed required technical specifications. Compliance with all required features (to include realism of the training, system flexibility, and performance-measurement tools). Quote meets warranty term requirements. Quote verifies compliance with all requested equipment/quantities, utilizing Exhibit A, �Technical Specs�. 2) Delivery Timeline. 3) International Deployment Experience and Maintenance/Support Coverage in Europe: The entity demonstrating International Deployment Experience and Maintenance/Support Coverage in Europe. 4) Past Performance: The entity demonstrates relevant past performance in at least three (3) contracts of similar or superior characteristics to those of this project. 5) Price: The overall price will be considered, and the lowest price is favorable.

title: REMEDIATION AND RESTORATION ACTIVITIES
description: Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Department of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Facilities Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program. As part of this effort, a Remedial Action (RA) will be conducted at one facility in the FAA Eastern Service Area (ESA) to remove identified soil contamination. The site requiring remediation for lead- and polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-contaminated soils is QPI RCAG � Matawan, NJ (40.370895�,-74.220954�). The FAA�s ECU Program has identified the potential for environmental and human health risks and/or liability associated with the facility above based on prior research, known historic operations and practices, and required cleanup actions. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State, and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. The Contractor shall submit a draft Remediation and Restoration work plan (Work Plan) (where applicable) within ten (10) business days of the project kick-off meeting that addresses the project requirements below. This task involves the preparation and submission of a draft and final Work Plan. The Work Plan shall detail the technical approach and schedule for conducting all contaminated soil remediation, disposal, and site restoration activities described below. To assist with preparation of the Work Plan, the contractor shall thoroughly review the Government-furnished information (GFI) for pertinent information. The removal quantities and depths in the Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation and Remedial Investigation reports (if provided) are to be used as a guide along with the estimated total quantities listed in this SOW Section 2.2.2. The Work Plan shall describe methods and procedures for performing soil remediation, disposal, and restoration. Disposal methods must be detailed by the contractor for the site. FAA has consulted a Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP), and the LSRP will select and approve all disposal facilities where waste and debris is to be shipped. Disposal sampling and paperwork is the responsibility of the contractor. Confirmatory sampling has already been conducted at the site. Additionally, the work plan shall also identify any required permits needed to perform the work. Futhermore, components required with the Work Plan are the Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP), which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed. The work plan shall also include a brief Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards on each site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. An outline summarizing the required content of the work plan is Technical Approach (Method and procedures for soil remediation, removal, disposal a. Identification of required work permits and b. Site Safety Health Plan (SSHP). Risk Management Plan a. Identification of major risks and b.Risk mitigation plan. The contractor should expect a 5-business day Volpe Center review period between submission of the Draft Work Plan and receipt of Volpe Center comments. The Volpe Center and the Contractor shall meet to discuss any comments and changes, if necessary. The contractor shall make the changes and submit a Final Work Plan within 5 business days of the receipt of comments. Contaminated Soil Remediation: Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation (PA/SI) and Remedial Investigation (RI) activities completed between 2020 and 2025 found soils at the below site containing contamination above FAA�s action levels, which are based on U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and/or New Jersey Residential Soil Remediation Standards. Examples include lead-in-soil concentrations above 200 mg/kg (ppm) or PCB-in-soil concentrations above 0.25 mg/kg. See SOW for greater details.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Responses will assist the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in identifying qualified sources and determining an appropriate acquisition strategy for Lean transformation and High Reliability Organization (HRO) consulting, training, coaching, and implementation support for the Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS). title: Q517--PHARMACY BENEFITS SERVICES | WICHITA |
description: QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS Q: Please clarify whether prescription drug ingredient costs reimbursed to participating retail pharmacies are considered pass-through costs or included in the 50% limitations on subcontracting calculation, and whether pharmacy dispensing fees are treated differently. A: This procurement is a services contract subject to the limitations on subcontracting requirements in VAAR 852.219-75. Prescription drug ingredient costs reimbursed to participating retail pharmacies are considered pass-through/direct reimbursement costs and are not considered service performance costs for purposes of the 50% subcontracting calculation. Pharmacy dispensing fees, however, are compensation for pharmacy services performed and are included in the limitations on subcontracting analysis unless performed by a similarly situated certified SDVOSB subcontractor. Offerors remain responsible for ensuring compliance with all applicable SBA and VA limitations on subcontracting requirements.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Objectives: The objective of the contemplated SRS acquisition is to provide FDA with responsive, high-quality scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the task order, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and nonclinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. The Government is interested in sources capable of providing the scientific depth and operational capacity needed to: Conduct scientifically sound analyses and prepare defensible, traceable technical products supporting FDA review and public-health decisions. Provide qualified personnel across multiple scientific and regulatory disciplines, including specialized and emerging areas. Support clinical and nonclinical study-data review, standardized scientific datasets, statistical computing, data fitness, quality assessment, and interpretation. Respond to multiple simultaneous task orders, changing priorities, time-sensitive scientific questions, and evolving requirements across FDA organizations. Maintain scientific quality, data integrity, documentation, confidentiality, and continuity of performance. Deliver effective scientific training, technical writing, knowledge transfer, and program-management support tied directly to scientific and regulatory missions. Project Requirements: The following descriptions are illustrative of the types of services that may be ordered. They are provided to inform industry responses and do not establish final task-order requirements. Each task order would define its own objectives, tasks, deliverables, performance expectations, staffing qualifications, and period of performance. Scientific Research and Regulatory Review Support: Support scientific investigations, literature and evidence reviews, research planning, study design, methodological assessments, scientific consultations, and technical analyses relevant to FDA-regulated products. Prepare scientific assessments, briefing materials, review support documentation, and other products that allow Government scientists and reviewers to evaluate scientific evidence and communicate findings. Provide subject-matter expertise to address complex or emerging regulatory science questions. Clinical and Nonclinical Study-Data Review and Analysis: Support the scientific review of clinical and nonclinical datasets submitted for regulatory purposes, including data fitness and completeness assessments, exploratory safety analyses, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, and preparation of tables, listings, figures, and visualizations. Experience with standards such as CDISC SDTM, ADaM, and SEND may be relevant. The RRS BPA describes review-oriented services that assess study data and produce analyses for FDA reviewers; SRS would focus on the scientific and analytical performance of those services rather than maintenance of the underlying software platforms. Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Pharmacovigilance, and Surveillance: Conduct epidemiological and Pharmacoepidemiological research, biostatistical analyses, pharmacovigilance assessments, signal detection and evaluation, public-health surveillance, and interpretation of real-world data and evidence as required by individual scientific programs. Activities may include protocol and analysis-plan support, assessment of study limitations and bias, statistical programming, results interpretation, and technical reporting. Scientific Data Standards, Quality, and Analytics: Provide scientific expertise related to data standards, controlled terminology, study-data interpretation, data quality and fitness, and reproducible analytical methods. Support scientific data preparation and validation, biostatistics, bioinformatics, computational science, and other specialized analyses when the primary deliverable is scientific or regulatory in nature. Distinguish these activities from enterprise database administration, application development, platform engineering, and IT operations. Laboratory and Specialized Scientific Support: Provide laboratory-related scientific and technical expertise, research assistance, analytical method support, study coordination, quality documentation, and interpretation or reporting of laboratory findings where required by a task order. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico.
