title: PANDHA-26-P-0000 046239 Security Support Services
description: The Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR), Europe Middle East (E-ME) has a continued cost share obligation for security services with the L. Sakvarelidze National Center for Disease Control and Public Health (NCDC) at the Richard G. Lugar Center for Public Health Research in the Republic of Georgia. The purpose of this contract is to provide cost share reimbursement for security support services throughout the Lugar Center. In accordance with the Implementing Agreement between the WRAIR and NCDC, dated 15 December 2015, Paragraph 5, Responsibilities, subparagraph (a)(6) state that the WRAIR will contract with NCDC to pay 50% of the Lugar Center�s cost that can be directly attributed to the operation and maintenance of the facility. NCDC is the sole legal Georgian entity responsible for the acquisition and payment of security services for the Lugar Center. As occupants of the Lugar Center, the WRAIR-E-ME is responsible for up to 50% of costs of these services. which will be based on the total amount invoiced and the payment amount to the service provider minus Georgia Value Added Tax. As the WRAIR, E-ME is not a legal Georgia entity and is only co-located at the facility, it cannot enter into a legally binding agreement to purchase and pay for security services outside of the services currently being provided by NCDC.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 2nd Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise resulting from responses to this RF

Synopsis � Chemical Sampling and Testing of Dredged Material for USACE New York District
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, New York District (NYD) intends to issue a solicitation package seeking to award one Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the Chemical Testing of Dredged Material. The IDIQ contract would include the sampling and testing of dredged material proposed for placement at the Historic Area Remediation Site (HARS). HARS sampling and testing would adhere to the procedures, and their subsequent updates, as described in: 2016 US Army Corps of Engineers New York District/EPA Region 2 Guidance for Performing Tests on Dredged Material Proposed for Ocean Disposal (a.k.a. Regional Testing Manual) (http://www.nan.usace.army.mil/Portals/37/docs/regulatory/Formdoc/FINAL_NYD-R2_REGIONAL_TESTINGMANUAL-APRIL%202016.pdf) 1991 EPA/USACE, Evaluation of Dredged Material Proposed for Ocean Disposal (a.k.a. the Green Book) (https://www.epa.gov/sites/production/files/2015-10/documents/green_book.pdf). The IDIQ contract would also include the sampling and testing of dredged material proposed for upland placement. �Upland� sampling and testing would adhere to the procedures, and their subsequent updates, as described in: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) New Jersey Administrative Code (NJAC), Title 7, Chapters 9 and 26 (a.k.a. �NJAC 7�) (https://dep.nj.gov/rules/current-rules-and-regulations/) New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) manual, entitled �Technical & Operational Guidance Series (TOGS) 5.1.9 In-Water and Riparian Management of Sediment and Dredged Material� (November 2004) (a.k.a. �TOGS 5.1.9�) (https://www.dec.ny.gov/docs/water_pdf/togs519.pdf) New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, New York Codes, Rules and Regulations (NYCRR), Title 6, Part 375 (December 2025) (a.k.a. �6 NYCRR Part 375�) (https://dec.ny.gov/sites/default/files/2025-12/6nycrrpart375final.pdf). Other state procedures may also be requested and would be coordinated between NYD and the contractor to determine capabilities. Additional work under this contract will include analyses of sediment, tissue, and water and may include environmental DNA/metagenomic analyses related to HARS monitoring in accordance with the following document and any subsequent updates: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) New York District and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2, Site Management and Monitoring Plan for Historic Area Remediation Site (HARS) (July 2020). Task orders would include all or some of the following: sediment and water collection (on Contractor-supplied ship) handling, processing and shipping of samples physical and chemical analyses quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) procedures, and necessary corrective actions. For each task order, the contractor would provide reports containing the sampling logs, all testing results and QA/QC information in the format required by NYD, EPA � Region 2, and/or state agencies. In addition to sampling and testing for ocean placement, NYD also requires that contractors be capable of performing testing procedures such as the Synthetic Precipitation Leaching Procedure (SPLP), the Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP), and the Modified Elutriate Test (MET), which are required for upland placement of dredged material in the states of New York and New Jersey. Prior to sampling and testing, a Work/Quality Assurance (QA) Plan and an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) would need to be prepared by the contractor and approved by NYD. A Work/QA Plan must include: descriptions of all technical procedures for field sampling, laboratory analyses (e.g. biological, physical) for HARS and upland testing, data reduction and validation, and reporting clearly written standard operating procedures (SOP) for all field, experimental and analytical procedures clearly defined QA objectives that are consistent with the regulations (e.g. Regional Testing Manual, Green Book, NJAC 7, TOGS 5.1.9, and 6 NYCRR Part 375) and if applicable, permit application mechanisms for conducting performance and systems audits during the course of the field laboratory work procedures for detecting problems with sampling and analytical work, and implementation of corrective actions in a timely manner. All sampling would be performed within the Port of New York & New Jersey, all Federal Navigation Channels within New York District, the length of the Hudson River, in the Atlantic Ocean at the Historic Area Remediation Site and its Mud Dump Reference Site. �New Work or Harbor Deepening� projects may be proposed and coordinated between NYD and the contractor. A detailed description of work required for these contracts will be provided in its entirety upon issuance of the complete solicitation. Prior to issuance of the solicitation, it is highly recommended that interested parties read the required regulations (e.g. Regional Testing Manual, Green Book, NJAC 7, TOGS 5.1.9, and 6 NYCRR Part 375) in order to obtain a thorough understanding of the work required by the NYD and EPA � Region 2 dredged material testing program. The Period of Performance will be five (5) years from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The contract magnitude will be up to $10,000,000.00 for five (5) years � up to $2,000,000.00 each year. One contract will be awarded on an Unrestricted Full and Open Competition basis to the lowest bidder who has, within the last 18 months, demonstrated their capability of performing the program�s work to EPA � Region 2. A bidder can prove their capability through one of the following: the bidder has received, within the last 18 months from EPA � Region 2, documentation stating that the laboratory has submitted data that is fully acceptable or acceptable with qualification; or the bidder has satisfied the Demonstration of Capability (DOC) requirements for the NYD and EPA � Region 2 dredged material testing program. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541380. The business size standard is $25,500,000.

description: **AMMENDMENT 1. REMOVED INCORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION AND UPLOADED CORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION*** **AMMENDMENT 2. UPDATED TERMS AND CONDITIONS. ADDED 52.217-9 AND REMOVED 52.226-3. **** The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to establish a contract for the provision of Grease Trap Cleaning Services. Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. Place of Performance Place of Performance will be located at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59 Lewis Run, PA 16738. Schedule The contractor will provide grease trap cleaning and waste disposal at the scheduled times below. The specific days for performance of these services will be established after contract award. The contractor will be required to provide these services on an estimated two to three month interval between the hours of 7:30AM-3:00PM, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays. The exact intervals between cleanings will be determined as needed by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). FCI McKean has one 10,000 gallon trap within the secure confines behind the Food Service department, and one 2,000 gallon trap at the satellite prison camp. All grease and pumpings removed shall be disposed of in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The contractor shall furnish an invoice for each service delivered at the time of extraction. All extractions and cleanings will be verified and signed for by an authorized representative. Specific Requirements The contractor will be licensed/permitted by the State of Pennsylvania and will provide evidence of proper waste disposal, in accordance with all current Federal, State, and local codes, laws, and requirements regarding the disposal of solid waste. Supplies and Equipment The contractor will provide the truck, labor, and equipment necessary for effective removal, transportation/disposal of waste. All material located within the container upon removal become the property and responsibility of the contractor to dispose of in a lawful manner. Description of Duties The contractor has sole responsibility and discretion for choosing and implementing the manner and method of performing tasks outlined in the Statement of Work as long as the requirements are met in accordance with the policies described above. The services, although not directly supervised, shall be reviewed by institution staff to ensure contract compliance. Contractor performance will be monitored by the COR and evaluated in accordance with FAR Part 42. Institution Security The contractor agrees to adhere to all regulations prescribed by the institution for the safety, custody, and conduct of inmates. Access to the containers will be available only during the scheduled hours, unless prior approval of the COR is obtained. All contract personnel that are entering the secure confines of the institution are required to have a clear NCIC background check.While on institution grounds and prior to departure, the operator, equipment, and vehicle shall be subject to security checks and inspections. The Government reserves the right for security reasons to prohibit certain vendor employees from entering the facility. Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in performance of work may be expected. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other security matters. When the contractor reports to the institution on a scheduled pickup but is unable to performance services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for their time in the form of a predetermined trip fee. The unperformed pickup may be rescheduled at the BOP�s discretion or may be performed on the next regularly scheduled pickup. Charges for the trip fee should be represented as separate line item charges on each invoice. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Matthew Morris, PPS, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3420 and/or Alyssa Mcgrew at (814)362 8900 extension 3422. Offers are due no later than November 23, 2026 at 2:00PM EST. Completed offers must be emailed to m4morris@bop.gov and amcgrew@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is December 4, 2026.

description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Objectives: The objective of the contemplated SRS acquisition is to provide FDA with responsive, high-quality scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the task order, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and nonclinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. The Government is interested in sources capable of providing the scientific depth and operational capacity needed to: Conduct scientifically sound analyses and prepare defensible, traceable technical products supporting FDA review and public-health decisions. Provide qualified personnel across multiple scientific and regulatory disciplines, including specialized and emerging areas. Support clinical and nonclinical study-data review, standardized scientific datasets, statistical computing, data fitness, quality assessment, and interpretation. Respond to multiple simultaneous task orders, changing priorities, time-sensitive scientific questions, and evolving requirements across FDA organizations. Maintain scientific quality, data integrity, documentation, confidentiality, and continuity of performance. Deliver effective scientific training, technical writing, knowledge transfer, and program-management support tied directly to scientific and regulatory missions. Project Requirements: The following descriptions are illustrative of the types of services that may be ordered. They are provided to inform industry responses and do not establish final task-order requirements. Each task order would define its own objectives, tasks, deliverables, performance expectations, staffing qualifications, and period of performance. Scientific Research and Regulatory Review Support: Support scientific investigations, literature and evidence reviews, research planning, study design, methodological assessments, scientific consultations, and technical analyses relevant to FDA-regulated products. Prepare scientific assessments, briefing materials, review support documentation, and other products that allow Government scientists and reviewers to evaluate scientific evidence and communicate findings. Provide subject-matter expertise to address complex or emerging regulatory science questions. Clinical and Nonclinical Study-Data Review and Analysis: Support the scientific review of clinical and nonclinical datasets submitted for regulatory purposes, including data fitness and completeness assessments, exploratory safety analyses, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, and preparation of tables, listings, figures, and visualizations. Subject-matter expertise in applicable clinical and nonclinical study-data standards, including CDISC SDTM, ADaM, and SEND, is particularly relevant to these services. The RRS BPA describes review-oriented services that assess study data and produce analyses for FDA reviewers; SRS would focus on the scientific and analytical performance of those services rather than maintenance of the underlying software platforms. Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Pharmacovigilance, and Surveillance: Conduct epidemiological and Pharmacoepidemiological research, biostatistical analyses, pharmacovigilance assessments, signal detection and evaluation, public-health surveillance, and interpretation of real-world data and evidence as required by individual scientific programs. Activities may include protocol and analysis-plan support, assessment of study limitations and bias, statistical programming, results interpretation, and technical reporting. Scientific Data Standards, Quality, and Analytics: Provide scientific expertise related to data standards, controlled terminology, study-data interpretation, data quality and fitness, and reproducible analytical methods. Support scientific data preparation and validation, biostatistics, bioinformatics, computational science, and other specialized analyses when the primary deliverable is scientific or regulatory in nature. Distinguish these activities from enterprise database administration, application development, platform engineering, and IT operations. Laboratory and Specialized Scientific Support: Provide laboratory-related scientific and technical expertise, research assistance, analytical method support, study coordination, quality documentation, and interpretation or reporting of laboratory findings where required by a task order. Respondents should identify the specific laboratory disciplines, facilities, qualifica

title: USCG ISA Tenant Improvement Construction Project
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation or a request for proposal and no contract will be awarded from this notice. No solicitation or specifications are available at this time. Please monitor sam.gov as this Sources Sought Notice will not be linked to the solicitation. The General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery Division, is conducting market research to determine if any SDVOSB, HUB Zone, EDWOSB or 8(a) Small Business Concern has the current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform the work described herein. All interested Small Business firms should respond. This Sources Sought Notice is being issued by the General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery for tenant fit-out Construction services for the United States Coast Guard (USCG) Northeast District to support mission-critical operations across the Northeast maritime region. The place of performance will be the John F. Kennedy (JFK) Federal Building (FB), located at 15 New Sudbury St, Boston, MA 02203. This is a Repair and Alteration (R&A) project which includes operational, administrative, secure, forensic, and mission-support spaces, with construction of a specialized Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) being a particularly important element. Work also includes integrated mission-specific systems such as reliable power, 24/7 HVAC, communications/IT infrastructure, security systems, laboratory support, resilient infrastructure, and an emergency generator. Contractors should anticipate a complex, schedule-sensitive federal fit-out requiring secure construction practices, specialized space coordination, and close integration of architectural, mechanical, electrical, communications, security, and technology systems. Estimated Construction Cost Range is $15,000,000 and $25,000,000.00. Period of Performance is approximately 36 months from date of Notice to Proceed. NAICS Code: Construction of Buildings - 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a size standard of $45 Million. PSC Code: Z2AA -- Repair or Alteration of Office Buildings All qualified Small Businesses are encouraged to respond. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The main purposes of this Sources Sought Notice is to assist the Contracting Officer in determining if a Set-Aside is the acceptable strategy for the procurement. It is requested that interested parties submit a brief capabilities package. The package shall address, at a minimum, the following: Examples of projects worked within the last five years of similar size, scope, complexity and duration as the work indicated. State whether your firm worked as a prime or subcontractor, contract value, brief description of how the referenced contract relates to the work described and provide an agency or owner point of contact. Company profile, to include number of employees, annual receipts, office location(s), and SAM UEI. Evidence to establish your company's standing as a SDVOSB, HUBZone, EDWOSB or 8(a) small business concern, under applicable NAICS. Describe how you will provide a fair market price given the geographical location of this project. A positive statement of your intention to submit a bid for this requirement if set-aside for your socio-economic group. AGAIN, THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. Responses must contain sufficient detail for the Government to make an informed decision regarding your capabilities. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM, Local Time on November 23, 2026. Please submit your capability statement via e-mail to Molly A. Lewis, Contract Officer, at Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Questions regarding this notice may be addressed to Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Failure to submit all information requested will result in a contractor not being considered as an interested small business concern.

title: 136 Airlift Wing C-130J Aircraft Wash
description: The purpose of this sources sought notice is to gain knowledge of potential sources, locations, and methods. This notice is for planning purposes only. The 136th Airlift Wing, Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base, Fort Worth, Texas, intends to issue a solicitation and award of a contract or agreement to periodically wash C-130J model aircraft. All aircraft washing and cleaning procedures shall be performed in accordance with applicable Air Force Technical Orders, including TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3. Contractors shall be responsible for complying with all requirements contained within the applicable Technical Orders. Aircraft washes are to take place at an alternate location or utilize a method that allows for outdoor wash at NASJRB Fort Worth that includes collection of run-off in accordance with installation host Navy and environmental regulations. All interested parties shall submit a written response to this office, not to exceed three (3) pages, addressing the following information: Company name. Unique Entity ID (UEI) and/or CAGE Code. Location where washes would occur. A description of access requirements for the wash location. A description of prior experience with washing large aircraft, highlighting any military-type washes. Method for completing washes. Indoor or outdoor washes. Time required on location to complete washes. Availability to schedule washes at the convenience of the Government. Confirmation that all aircraft washing and cleaning procedures will be performed in accordance with TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3 Confirmation that only approved materials meeting MIL-PRF-87937 and MIL-PRF-85570 specifications will be used. NOTICE: Technical Orders 1C-130J-23CL-1 and 1C-130J-23S-3 contain distribution-restricted technical data and will not be provided as part of this Sources Sought Notice. Interested parties are not required to review these TOs for the purpose of responding to this notice. The requirements below identify the anticipated scope of work and key performance considerations applicable to C-130J aircraft exterior washing and corrosion control services. Any future contract award or agreement may require compliance with the current versions of applicable Technical Orders and Air Force guidance. Applicable Requirements for C-130J Aircraft Washes The contractor shall possess the capability to: Perform exterior aircraft washing of C-130J aircraft using approved aircraft cleaning methods, equipment, and materials suitable for military aircraft finishes and coatings. Utilize cleaning compounds, detergents, and wash procedures that are compatible with painted surfaces, transparencies, composite materials, antennas, sensors, and other aircraft components. Conduct freshwater rinsing procedures sufficient to remove contaminants, cleaning agents, salt deposits, dirt, oil, grease, hydraulic fluid residue, exhaust residue, and environmental pollutants. Prevent water intrusion into aircraft openings, vents, sensors, avionics components, pitot-static systems, and other sensitive areas during washing operations. Protect aircraft components and finishes from damage caused by improper washing techniques, excessive pressure, unauthorized chemicals, abrasive materials, or improper equipment use. Identify, document, and report visible signs of corrosion, coating deterioration, surface damage, fluid leaks, paint degradation, or other discrepancies observed during wash operations. Comply with all applicable Foreign Object Damage (FOD) prevention requirements while performing aircraft wash operations. Comply with all applicable environmental, hazardous material, hazardous waste, stormwater, and occupational safety regulations associated with aircraft washing activities. Provide trained and qualified personnel familiar with military aircraft washing, corrosion prevention, corrosion detection, and corrosion reporting practices. Furnish all labor, supervision, tools, equipment, cleaning materials, personal protective equipment, and transportation necessary to perform aircraft wash services. Maintain documentation of completed wash services and any corrosion or maintenance discrepancies identified during performance. Demonstrate the capability to perform aircraft washing services in a manner that supports corrosion prevention and preservation of aircraft structural integrity, protective coatings, and mission readiness. In the event that Small Business contractors are not available for adequate competition for this requirement, it may be advertised as unrestricted. Information shall be submitted via email to 136.AW.MSC@us.af.mil. Include the following subject line: �Sources Sought � Aircraft Washes � Your Company Name.� No facsimile responses will be accepted. description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS FOR A DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT TO RENOVATE THE UNACCOMPANIED ENLISTED PERSONNEL HOUSING QUARTERS (BUILDINGS 1042, 1044, 1045, 1046 AND 1054) LOCATED AT NAVAL SUBMARINE BASE (SUBBASE) KINGS BAY, GA. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The reference number for this posting is N6945027RUPHR. The purpose of this notice is for the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southeast (NAVFAC SE) to gain knowledge of ALL qualified and interested parties. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), SBA certified HUBZone, woman-owned small business (WOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), and service disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB). Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform this proposed project. The Government may use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement. Project Description: This project will include, but is not limited to, renovate the Unaccompanied Enlisted Personnel Housing Quarters (Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045, 1046 and 1054) located at Naval Submarine Base (SUBBASE), Kings Bay, Georgia. Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045 and 1046 were constructed in 1984. Building 1054 was constructed in 1989. The project scope includes upgrades to mechanical systems, fire protection, fire alarms, bathrooms, and exterior renovation. Except for Air Handling Units (AHU) in Buildings 1042, 1044 and 1046, all mechanical systems are being upgraded under this project. Mechanical system repairs include replacement of HVAC AHUs, installing Direct Digital Controls (DDC) for temperature and humidity, replacement of chilled water (CHW) piping, circulation pumps and cleaning of ductwork. Plumbing repairs include the replacement of plumbing fixtures, domestic water piping and sanitary piping. Electrical system repairs include replacement of electrical service panels throughout the building. Electrical repairs also include replacement of lighting fixtures with LED fixtures and replacement of wiring and wiring devices where they do not meet the current codes. Exterior renovation includes replacement of gutters, windows, doors, safety railings, lights. Interior renovation includes remodeling of bathrooms, mold remediation, and cleaning and painting of all previously painted surfaces. Ceilings and non-loadbearing walls will be demolished and rebuilt as required to allow access to rebuild mechanical and plumbing ductwork and pipes. The project also requires the design for abatement of hazardous material. The hazardous materials survey has been conducted by the industrial hygiene professionals, and the findings of the survey are included in the report. The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 1200 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000. The anticipated award date is fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this Sources Sought announcement. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at $20 million or greater and/or 30,000 square feet or greater. Completed within the past seven (7) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including contract number, project title, completion date, performance ratings, and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. Please respond to this announcement no later than 23 NOV 2026, 2:00 PM Eastern Time via email to Darrien Thomas at darrien.a.thomas.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson at aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. The subject line of the email shall state: Unaccompanied Personnel Housing Restoration, NSB Kings Bay. Emails shall be no more than 5 MB in size. Supplies and Equipment The contractor will provide the truck, labor, and equipment necessary for effective removal, transportation/disposal of waste. All material located within the container upon removal become the property and responsibility of the contractor to dispose of in a lawful manner. Description of Duties The contractor has sole responsibility and discretion for choosing and implementing the manner and method of performing tasks outlined in the Statement of Work as long as the requirements are met in accordance with the policies described above. The services, although not directly supervised, shall be reviewed by institution staff to ensure contract compliance. Contractor performance will be monitored by the COR and evaluated in accordance with FAR Part 42. Institution Security The contractor agrees to adhere to all regulations prescribed by the institution for the safety, custody, and conduct of inmates. Access to the containers will be available only during the scheduled hours, unless prior approval of the COR is obtained. All contract personnel that are entering the secure confines of the institution are required to have a clear NCIC background check.While on institution grounds and prior to departure, the operator, equipment, and vehicle shall be subject to security checks and inspections. The Government reserves the right for security reasons to prohibit certain vendor employees from entering the facility. Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in performance of work may be expected. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other security matters. When the contractor reports to the institution on a scheduled pickup but is unable to performance services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for their time in the form of a predetermined trip fee. title: Manufacture of M284A2 155mm and other MTC Cannon Tubes
description: Purpose: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island (ACC-RI) at Picatinny, Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806-5000 is conducting a Market Survey on behalf of the Project Manager Howitzer Systems (PM-HS). PM-HS has a need to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing the M284A2 155mm, and other 155mm cannon tubes domestically in specific quantities and lead time annotated below. The purpose of this market research is to obtain current information on the capability of additional sources to manufacture 155mm Cannon Tubes up to 30-foot length. No other data or drawings will be provided with this Market Survey. Description: The .39 caliber, 155-mm M776 and M284A2 cannon tubes are components of the M777A2 and M109A6/A7 Howitzers respectively. 155-mm cannons are direct support cannon fire support system for the U.S. Army and must be built to the United States Government technical data specifications. This Sources Sought is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the US Government. All interested respondents are requested to provide a written response summarizing the following capabilities and organizational details. Manufacturers with domestic capacity in the works are also encouraged submit their response along with their prospective production timetables. Please clarify if respondent�s capabilities apply to one or all the cannon tube models. REQUESTED: 1. Name of company, address, telephone number, email address, technical point of contact, CAGE code, UEI, and business size information (please specify as either a Large Business, Foreign-Owned Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a) concern, Woman-Owned Small Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone concern, Veteran-Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Small Business). 2. Experience: A description of the respondent�s manufacturing experience of the 155-mm Cannon Tubes, or similar products, within the last five (5) years to include past performance. Include applicable description of experience with each cannon tube. 3. Production Process: A description of the respondent�s existing 155-mm cannon production process to include all major manufacturing stages and the operations/equipment utilized for each, as well as all supporting subcontractors. The description must detail the entire production lifecycle, including, but not limited to: 3.1. A detailed description of the respondents bore and outside diameter cold working capabilities to include autofrettage. 3.2. A detailed description of the respondent�s boring and milling capabilities along with the capacity or each (length, weight, outer/inner diameters). 3.3. A detailed description of the respondent's rifling capabilities, including methods (e.g., swage, broach, or single-point machining) and general experience with standard 155-mm rifling configurations (lands, grooves, and twist rates). 3.4. A detailed description of the respondent or subcontractor coating capabilities for chrome bore coatings on a steel tube up to 30 ft long and up to 7,500 pounds in weight. Provide the maximum length and weight of tube that can be coated by respondent. 3.5. A detailed description of the respondent�s protective coating and painting capabilities. 3.6. Detailed description of the respondent�s advanced manufacturing capabilities and growth areas. 4. Production Capacity: A description of the respondent�s current maximum monthly capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes. Please specify separate production rate capacity for each and if different manufacturing lines, tooling, or subcontractors are utilized. 5. Production Availability: A description of the respondent�s maximum caliber capability and projected available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes within 18 months from the date of these sources sought. 6. Optimization opportunity: A description of the domestic facilities, equipment, machines and tooling required to increase the available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes up to ten (10) tubes per month, regardless of caliber, within 36 months from the date of this source sought. Specify whether the projected production capacity for each tube type is dedicated or shared across multiple lines. Provide an NTE ROM cost estimate for an initial production quantity of forty (40) cannon tubes (broken down by caliber or indicating pricing for a combined/flexible mix). 7. Material: A detailed description of the respondent�s cannon tube source material grade, respondent(s) and processing. Such as, but not limited to, steel preform production, forging, guide bore, and heat treatment. title: Optometrist Services - OAX
description: Please see the following Q&A. What malpractice insurance limits are required? Is $1,000,000 per claim and $2,000,000 aggregate acceptable? Yes, this is acceptable or whatever your state requires. Attachment 1, Part D says at least 50% of personnel costs must go to the quoter�s own employees, while Section I cites FAR 52.219-14. Which rule applies? The Business Questionnaire was not updated, but it should reflect FAR 52.219-14 (DEV), which states the following: (e)(1) Services (except construction), it will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor's 50 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded. When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50 percent limitation shall apply only to the service portion of the contract; Would an optometrist engaged through a qualifying small business count toward our share? No, since you are both of the same small business entity, it wouldn�t. See reference. (b) Definition. Similarly situated entity, as used in this clause, means a first-tier subcontractor, including an independent contractor, that� (1) Has the same small business program status as that which qualified the prime contractor for the award (e.g., for a small business set-aside contract, any small business concern, without regard to its socioeconomic status); and (2) Is considered small for the size standard under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code the prime contractor assigned to the subcontract. The Statement of Work mentions a BPA, while Section G describes a requirements contract. Which type of award will this be? That�s a typo�BPA�s are associated with GSA FSS. Contracts are associated with SAM. Must the quote include a signed SF 1449 Block 30? It�s optional because the quote is not an offer for an award. Does the �Schedule of Supplies/Services (pp 42-43)� mean the Section B pages 5 and 6? Yes, that is correct. Does FCC Oakdale provide the exam equipment, supplies, frames and lenses, so the contractor provides only the optometrist? Please refer to the SOW for it should state what the institution will provide and if the vendor needs to provide anything. If releasable, what was the unit price per session under the previous contract, 15B51821D00000520, and how many sessions were ordered each year? The qty is 576 SS and $250/ss. THIS IS AN EXISTING REQUIREMENT � Services were in place for this requirement, but expired September 30, 2026. The award number is 15B51821D00000520 and the incumbent was National Eye Care. At present, no services are being provided. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for the provision of Optometrist Services for FCC Oakdale, located in Oakdale, LA, prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), Field Acquisition Office (FAO), intends to award an indefinite delivery/requirements type contract with firm-fixed unit pricing. The award will be based on price and past performance. The contract periods for the service will consist of a base year with four, 12-month option years, at the unilateral discretion of the Government. Solicitation number 15BGCS27Q51800001 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) and is being solicited as total small business concerns. The North American Industrial Classification (NAICS) code is 621320. For all purposes of this solicitation, all quoter's SAM registration profile shall include NAICS code 621320. The solicitation document (RFQ), located in the Attachments/Links section, contains the Statement of Work (SOW), which provides a detailed description of the requirement(s) of the items/services being requested, a list of line-item number(s) with description of requested service, quantities and units of measure (including option(s), if applicable). The solicitation document incorporates most provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Quotations shall be completed, utilizing the attached Standard Form 1449 and any additional required forms, per the quote submission instructions. Quotes shall be submitted, on or before the solicitation deadline specified in Block 8 of the Standard Form 1449, via email, to LaShundra D. Thomas at ldthomas@bop.gov. Section L of the solicitation document provides detailed quote submission instructions, evaluation and award methodology information and any specific documentation requirements to be submitted along with the quote. All future information concerning this acquisition, including solicitation amendments/RFQ changes, will be distributed solely through this platform. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site, during the entire solicitation period, to ensure you have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. Failure to provide all quotation requirements on most up to date RFQ may result in your quote being eliminated from consideration for award. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The website provides all downloading instructions to obtain a copy of the solicitation. All contractors doing business with the Federal Government are advised that this future solicitation includes the provision at FAR 52.204-7, System for Award Management (SAM). This provision requires all contractors doing business with the federal government to be registered in the SAM database for �All Awards�. Quoters shall include their Unique Entity Identification Number (UEI) number in their quotes. The Contracting Officer will verify registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to award by entering the potential awardees UEI number into the SAM database. Failure to complete the registration procedures outlined in provision may result in elimination from consideration for award. If you have questions regarding the System for Award Management (SAM), Government procurements in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your quote, the APEX Accelerators program may be able to help. title: Chief Joseph Dam Main Unit XJ Breaker Disconnects Modernization
description: EVENT DETAILS: Date: 3 December 2026 Time: 0930-1430 PT Format: Presentation & Site walk Registration Due Date: 23 November 2026, 1200 PT; Please register by returning completed Request for Visit Authority (RVA) by email to: Sarah Malowicki, Project Manager, at sarah.m.malowicki@usace.army.mil, AND Londres Medranda, Contract Specialist, at londres.medranda@usace.army.mil. Confirmation email will be sent upon receipt of completed RVA. Who Should Attend: Interested vendors, including small businesses, large businesses, and other industry partners. Attendance is limited to 2 personnel per company. Attendance is limited to United States Citizens. Attendance at this event is not mandatory. Pre-registration is required. DESCRIPTION: In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(a) Early exchanges with industry, the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District (NWS) is hosting an Industry Day on 3 December 2026 at Chief Joseph Dam in Bridgeport, Washington. This Industry Day provides an opportunity for interested parties to inspect the existing 15.5KV Main Unit XJ Breaker disconnects first-hand. By hosting this first-hand inspection, the government aims to gather technical feedback and explore industry alternatives for modernizing this equipment. We are seeking input from qualified, experienced sources, capable of performing this modernization work. PROJECT BACKGROUND: At Chief Joseph Dam the current Unit 1-16 XJ Breaker disconnects are original BBC (Brown Boveri Corporation) equipment and rated 6000A according to the BBC shop drawings. The switch operators are pneumatically driven, and are actuated by operation of a complex key interlocking scheme with the circuit breaker. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously operated by a single shared pneumatic actuating system. The current Units 17-27 breaker disconnects are original GE equipment. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously controlled by mechanically operated hand crank. USACE is evaluating options to improve reliability, maintainability, remote-operating capability, and overall generating-unit availability. � Option 1: Refurbish and restore existing disconnect switches to an approved condition equivalent to original design intent, as technically feasible. Integrate motorized mechanisms on the switch arms to enable remote operation, and comprehensively overhaul and test the existing main unit breakers to ensure optimal system protection. � Option 2: Replace the disconnect switches with new electrically operated units and refurbish the existing breakers. � Option 3: Replace both the disconnect switches (with new electrically operated units) and the main unit circuit breakers. � Option 4: Replace the entire switchgear assembly with new enclosures, modern electrically operated disconnect switches, and new circuit breakers (includes associated controls, protection, buswork and new enclosure). Chief Joseph Dam has several critical limitations that affect this project, primarily related to space constraints. This Industry day will present the options under consideration, obtain industry feedback on technical feasibility and constructability, and identify potential risks, constraints and cost drivers. USACE is requesting feedback on the following questions and relevant, non-binding information: Does your company have the ability, capacity, interest and willingness to perform the proposed options? Does your company have experience with comparable medium-voltage/high-current generation-station disconnect and breaker modernization projects? We are not currently requiring quotes or bids, however rough estimates would be greatly appreciated. Recommended technical approaches or alternatives Major schedule outage, access, safety, supply-chain or constructability risks. Do you believe all aspects of this requirement could be successfully performed by the small business sector under NAICS 237990 (Size standard $45M)? (Yes/No). If No, what estimated percentage do you think can be subcontracted out to small business? Small Business (SB) ______% Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) ________% Woman-Owned SB (WOSB) _______% Veteran Owned SB (VOSB) _______% Service Disabled VOSB (SDVOSB) _______% Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) _______% Important Notice: Attendance and participation is not required for consideration on future contracts related to this work. The U.S. Government is not obligated to pay for any information, documentation, demonstrations, or data provided, nor will it reimburse any costs incurred by your organization in preparing responses, traveling to, or participating in this Industry Day and physical equipment inspection. All costs associated with attending this event and participating in this information exchange are solely at the responding party�s expense. Small Business Program Inquiries: Enshane Hill-Nomoto: Enshane.Nomoto@usace.army.mil https://www.nws.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Small-Business/ Thank you for your interest in this USACE project.

description: ***This solicitation is a Small Business set-a-sided, restricted to 100% small business only.***The project includes repairs and upgrades to an existing fuel storage and dispensing facility. Work includes repairing concrete and pavement; removing water from an underground communications access box; installing an emergency fuel shutoff station and leak detection equipment; and repairing and recoating fuel system canopies, piping, and related components. Additional work includes replacing tank vents, repairing and improving grounding systems, modifying platforms to provide safe access to tank equipment, and upgrading the automatic tank gauging (ATG) system and associated controls.*****Proposal Due Date has been extended from 11/23/2026 to 12/21/2026 at 14:00 CST*****

description: THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ). This presolicitation notice is for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government to award a purchase order. The Department of the Interior (DOI), United States Geological Survey (USGS) Acquisition Team, seeks a qualified firm to perform an independent code review of the ShakeAlert Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) Production System. ShakeAlert is a mission-critical system that operates continuously to detect earthquakes and provide life-safety warnings to more than 50 million people along the U.S. West Coast. The production environment comprises numerous real-time, safety-critical software components that have evolved over many years and are maintained by a small team under significant operational constraints. The objective of this work is to improve the reliability, maintainability, and long-term sustainability of the ShakeAlert production code base through two complementary activities: - A rigorous, module-by-module review of source code quality, correctness, and maintainability. - An assessment of current software development and deployment practices, with concrete recommendations for modernizing the GitLab CI/CD pipeline and workflow. Work will be performed in phases over a period not to exceed 12 months. All work shall be conducted with regular coordination with USGS ShakeAlert staff. All work can be performed remotely. title: Industry Day: Chief Joseph Dam Main Unit XJ Breaker Disconnects Modernization
description: EVENT DETAILS: Date: 3 December 2026 Time: 0930-1430 PT Format: Presentation & Site walk Registration Due Date: 23 November 2026, 1200 PT; Please register by returning completed Request for Visit Authority (RVA) by email to: Sarah Malowicki, Project Manager, at sarah.m.malowicki@usace.army.mil, AND Londres Medranda, Contract Specialist, at londres.medranda@usace.army.mil. Confirmation email will be sent upon receipt of completed RVA. Who Should Attend: Interested vendors, including small businesses, large businesses, and other industry partners. Attendance is limited to 2 personnel per company. Attendance is limited to United States Citizens. Attendance at this event is not mandatory. Pre-registration is required. DESCRIPTION: In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(a) Early exchanges with industry, the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District (NWS) is hosting an Industry Day on 3 December 2026 at Chief Joseph Dam in Bridgeport, Washington. This Industry Day provides an opportunity for interested parties to inspect the existing 15.5KV Main Unit XJ Breaker disconnects first-hand. By hosting this first-hand inspection, the government aims to gather technical feedback and explore industry alternatives for modernizing this equipment. We are seeking input from qualified, experienced sources, capable of performing this modernization work. PROJECT BACKGROUND: At Chief Joseph Dam the current Unit 1-16 XJ Breaker disconnects are original BBC (Brown Boveri Corporation) equipment and rated 6000A according to the BBC shop drawings. The switch operators are pneumatically driven, and are actuated by operation of a complex key interlocking scheme with the circuit breaker. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously operated by a single shared pneumatic actuating system. The current Units 17-27 breaker disconnects are original GE equipment. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously controlled by mechanically operated hand crank. USACE is evaluating options to improve reliability, maintainability, remote-operating capability, and overall generating-unit availability. � Option 1: Refurbish and restore existing disconnect switches to an approved condition equivalent to original design intent, as technically feasible. Integrate motorized mechanisms on the switch arms to enable remote operation, and comprehensively overhaul and test the existing main unit breakers to ensure optimal system protection. � Option 2: Replace the disconnect switches with new electrically operated units and refurbish the existing breakers. � Option 3: Replace both the disconnect switches (with new electrically operated units) and the main unit circuit breakers. � Option 4: Replace the entire switchgear assembly with new enclosures, modern electrically operated disconnect switches, and new circuit breakers (includes associated controls, protection, buswork and new enclosure). Chief Joseph Dam has several critical limitations that affect this project, primarily related to space constraints. This Industry day will present the options under consideration, obtain industry feedback on technical feasibility and constructability, and identify potential risks, constraints and cost drivers. USACE is requesting feedback on the following questions and relevant, non-binding information: Does your company have the ability, capacity, interest and willingness to perform the proposed options? Does your company have experience with comparable medium-voltage/high-current generation-station disconnect and breaker modernization projects? title: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) - Buy and Repair F3I DTR
description: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources with the expertise, capabilities, experience, facilities, and technical capacity necessary to manufacture/provide and repair the B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR). The National Stock Number (NSN) and Part Number (PN) are as follows: LRU: NSN 7025-01-738-4504AY, P/N P210015K0001-1, INTERFACE UNIT, DATA This Request for Information (RFI) supports a buy and repair requirement for the new Form, Fit, Function, and Interface (F3I) DTR. Kihomac, Inc. is currently manufacturing the F3I DTR under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015. The Government owns, or will provide under appropriate controls, the manufacturing and technical data necessary to support competitive production and repair of this item. The Government intends to compete this requirement on the open market to obtain new production units and repair services. The legacy B-52 DTR is repaired by Symetrics Industries (CAGE 22830) under contracts FA8539-20-D-0013 and FA8539-25-D-0004. This market research effort pertains to the F3I DTR identified above, currently being manufactured by Kihomac, Inc. under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015, and is intended to identify sources capable of supporting competitive manufacture and repair using Government-owned technical data. The DTR is a Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) on the B-52 aircraft, with two DTRs installed per aircraft. The DTR transfers Offensive Avionics System (OAS) information to and from storage on the Data Transfer Cartridge (DTC) across its interface with the Fibre Channel or MIL-STD-1553A data bus system. Additionally, the DTR provides status over the MIL-STD-1553A and Fibre Channel buses indicating that the DTC is successfully installed. The required scope shall include, as applicable, manufacture and delivery of new production DTR units; hardware repair and return of unserviceable DTR units; obsolete parts resolution; engineering support to investigate Deficiency Reports (DRs); Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) support; development, maintenance, and execution of required inspection, test, and acceptance procedures; and configuration management support to ensure newly manufactured and repaired units conform to the applicable Government-furnished technical data package. All newly manufactured and repaired units must meet applicable form, fit, function, and interface requirements. The contractor shall furnish all necessary material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, facilities, and services required to perform the work. The contractor is responsible for acquiring, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at its primary or subcontractor facilities. Contractor-furnished material or replacement parts must equal or exceed the quality, tolerances, and specifications identified in the applicable technical data package. INSTRUCTIONS: 1. The document(s) below contain a description of the NSN listed for buy and repair requirements and a Contractor Capability Survey. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MULTI-SOURCE PNT UE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotations (RFQ)) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Due to the operational sensitivity of the Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) missions, any future acquisition resulting from this market research will require strict adherence to Department of War (DoW) and Department of Defense (DoD) security, cybersecurity, and supply chain integrity standards. Consequently, while direct responses to this RFI must remain entirely unclassified (reach out to the government contacts below for information on classified submissions), respondents are required to demonstrate their organizational posture regarding facility clearances, information safeguarding, and National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) supply chain compliance. For the purposes of this market research, the anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for manufacturing global positioning systems (GPS) and related equipment is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0 Million, and the primary Product Service Code (PSC) for Global Positioning Systems (GPS) hardware is 5825 (Radio Navigation Equipment, Except Airborne). For specialized, airborne GPS or radar navigation, the code is typically 5826. System-level R&D and engineering services for GPS are usually categorized under codes like R425 (Engineering Services) or AC13 (R&D�Defense System: Electronics). 2.0 BACKGROUND With advances in autonomous systems and guided munitions, the force that can best synchronize its activities at a single point in time and space wields a potent strategic advantage. In the future operating environment, therefore, the Joint Force will increasingly depend on resilient, reliable, and precise position, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to execute combat operations. As such, the Space Force is required to deliver global continuous coverage with stringent civil and military position and timing requirements to assure safety and mission success. This includes at least 88% of the constellation being operationally available more than 98% of the time. Likewise, a thinking adversary will make focused and deliberate efforts to deny access to this capability, leveraging a growing suite of threats including electromagnetic weapons, cyberspace attacks, and kinetic weapons. The challenge today is that, while satellite navigation (SATNAV) through the Global Positioning System (GPS) is foundational to U.S. military operations, critical infrastructure, and global commerce, the current architecture must adapt to evolving jamming and spoofing threats. Additionally, the space and ground segments must be modernized and hardened against physical attack. To build readiness for the future operating environment, therefore, the Space Force will pursue a comprehensive navigation warfare (NAVWAR) strategy that emphasizes resilience, technology modernization, modularity, adaptability, and flexibility. Specifically, it will adopt an open hybrid approach to SATNAV architecture that weighs inputs from diverse sources according to user need, generating a more dependable capability that can withstand adversary action while enabling faster upgrade cycles to enable PNT capabilities. The NAVWAR Objective Force pursues the development and deployment of several key capabilities to advance the SATNAV architecture. One of those elements is User Segment. To make best use of diversified PNT sources, the Space Force will enable a transition to a Multi-Source PNT user equipment (UE) reference architecture that incorporates Modular Open System Architectures (MOSA) and an onboard fusion engine to integrate all available data at the user level. The key enabler of the NAVWAR Objective Force is continued Joint Force investment in Multi-Source PNT UE that utilizes both traditional and new PNT sources. This equipment is foundational to a user�s ability to devise and execute a NAVWAR PACE (i.e., Primary / Alternate / Contingency / Emergency) Plan in degraded or denied environments. While legacy signals are expected to remain supported for civil and public functions, they are increasingly less effective in the contested environment. The military-specific M-Code is available today, while the PNT modernization signals are projected to be available by 2035. 3.0 OBJECTIVE, DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to analytical information on industrial capabilities in Multi-Source PNT UE the NAVWAR Objective Force. Interests include the following: Multi-Source PNT UE for Terrestrial Users on various military platforms Disadvantaged user High value military assets MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Space Service Volume Multi-Source PNT UE (various orbits) Small satellite users Large satellite users MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Interest is in technical details that can be incorporated into technical analysis to support Space Warfighting Analysis Center, Technology and Emerging Concept Assessments performed during Force Designs. This RFI is being executed in cooperation with the Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC). 4.0 SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY AND SUPPLY CHAIN REQUIREMENTS The secure nature of this requirement dictates adherence to stringent Department of War (DoW) / Department of Defense (DoD) security protocols. While direct responses to this RFI must remain unclassified, respondents shall address their current capabilities and compliance regarding the following security domains: a. Facility and Personnel Security Clearances Given the operational nature of Multi-Source PNT UE and the potential for integration with multiple military architectures, e?orts will likely require access to classified information and systems. Respondents must state their current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) (e.g., None, Secret, Top Secret) and classified safeguarding capabilities. Respondents should confirm their capacity to provide appropriately cleared personnel (Personnel Security Clearances - PCL) and facility infrastructure to support secure development, testing, and operations. Please indicate your facility's current capability and experience in handling, storing, and integrating Communications Security (COMSEC) and Transmission Security (TRANSEC) materials. b. Cybersecurity and Information Safeguarding (CUI/CDI) The protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Covered Defense Information (CDI) is critical to this effort. In accordance with DFARS 252.204-7012, 7019, and 7020, respondents must describe their current capability to safeguard CUI/CDI. The overall scope includes the GEP site civils, procurement, installation, integration, test and verification of GEP site communications shelters, antennas and antenna electronics, optical terminals and optical electronics, test hardware training and onsite test support, and GEP site networking equipment and software at multiple, globally dispersed locations. Proposals are due by 16:00 (4:00 PM) Eastern Time on 23 November 2026. Please refer to Section L, Proposal Instructions for more information and submission details. The complete RFP Package includes the following documents (note - CUI documents are only available upon request): RFP Cover Letter Attachment 1 RMWT LEO GEPs Base IDIQ SOW (CUI) Attachment 2 RMWT LEO GEPs Task Order 1 SOW (CUI) Attachment 3 RMWT LEO GEPs TRD (CUI) Attachment 4.a RMWT LEO GEPs IDIQ Contract Data Requirements List (CDRLS) Attachment 4.b RMWT LEO GEPs TO Contract Data Requirements List (CDRLS) Attachment 5.a RMWT LEO GEPs IDIQ Model Contract Attachment 5.b RMWT LEO GEPs TO Model Contract Attachment 6 RMWT LEO GEPs Ordering Procedures Attachment 7 RMWT LEO GEPs Section L Proposal Instructions 7a.
